J U D G M E N T / AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (North-West) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors.. Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 13 land for public purpose.

sentences.text: The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2631 Bighas and 04 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

sentences.text: The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2004/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2631 Bighas 04 Biswas land situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 25 of 2005-06 dated 06.02.2006 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2631 Bighas 04 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/- per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/- per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

Vs.
Union of India Page no. 5 of 13 having share situated in the revenue estate of Village K. S. Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi (as detailed in the Statement u/s 19 of LA Act) (in short, the said land).

5. It is stated that the award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and, therefore,
this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been arbitrarily assessed by the LAC without taking into account the fertility, potentiality, surroundings and topography under acquisition.

The said land is levelled land and is situated in a belt which has not experienced any major earthquake, flood or any other natural calamity and is best suited for all sorts of land uses like residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural etc. the quality of the said land makes it most suitable in the state of Delhi.

6. It is stated that the said land falls in the most fertile area and the petitioners are cultivating the said land and are growing three crops in a year "fasali year" and the income per acre is more than Rs. 2 lakhs per year.

7. It is stated that the petitioners shall be forced to change from one mode of life i.e. agro based lifestyle to modern lifestyle due to the acquisition of the said land and the new lifestyle has become more expensive, and the daily inflation shall have an adverse economic effect on the petitioners, who were self-reliant before acquisition of the said land.
The said land acquired by the ld.
LAC is surrounded by the residential as well as industrial areas.
The area under acquisition is having mettled roads, and is having a very good connectivity with other areas of Delhi.
The National Highway-10 is just 1 km away from LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors..
Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 13 the revenue estate of Village Kirari Patti Nithari and the railway line from Delhi Junction to Firozpur is just half kilometres away.

The infrastructure in the vicinity of the land of the petitioners is already in existence i.e. electricity, schools, residential areas and industrial areas, have been developed which has enhanced the market value of the said land.

8. It is stated that the land under acquisition including the said land is having better location than the revenue estate of Village like Karala, Sevda, Ghevra and Hiran Koodna which falls on the North-Western and South- Western side of the revenue estate of village Nithari, Delhi where sale Prem Singh Ors. (2505-06) vs Union Of India (K.S.Nagar, Patti ... on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76469977/
4 instances show constant rise in the land rates, however, those lands are far away from village Nithari, if the distance from the urban limits of Delhi state are taken into consideration.

The said land has great potentiality and is fit for supporting high rise buildings, and other residential infrastructure with a lesser investment, if compared with the development work carried out in South Delhi and East Delhi, where the land was hilly, terrain and low line respectively, which require a huge amount for levelling and making the land usable for construction activities.

The ld. LAC has overlooked the facts while determining the market value of the said land, in as much as, if all the factors are taken together for assessing the market value of the land under acquisition, it shall be Rs.
1 crore per acre or at least Rs. 2000/- per square yard.

If the said land under acquisition is auctioned to the private developers, they would have purchased the same for more than Rs. 1 crore per acre,
which fact finds support from the fact that the land bordering Delhi, particularly in the village Kundli and Kasar in Haryana, has shown a very fast increase in the land prices LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors..
Vs. Union of India Page no. 7 of 13
due to participation of private builders, however, the land of Village Kundli and Kasar is comparatively inferior to the land under acquisition.

9. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming market value of Rs. 2000/- per sq. yards or Rs. 1 crores per acre in addition to the said market value.
The petitioners have also claimed solatium @ 30% and additional amount @ 12% and further claim interest @ 9% and 15% as per the provisions of the Act.

10. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/UOI that the land was acquired for the purpose of PDD, therefore, DDA is a necessary and a proper party for the complete adjudication.

It is further stated that the reference under section 18 of the LA Act is time barred,
therefore, the reference is liable to be dismissed.
11.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to Ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

12. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/2005 06/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors..
Vs. Union of India Page no. 8 of 13 there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore, DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.

The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition Prem Singh Ors. (2505-06) vs Union Of India (K.S.Nagar, Patti ... on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76469977/
5 for enhancement of compensation.

It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioner is not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition are denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.

14. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 06.04.2017:-
LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors.. Vs. Union of India Page no. 9 of 13 ISSUES 1.

sentences.text: Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
OPP 2. Relief.
15. Matter was listed for recording of petitioner's evidence.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioners as well as Ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 459 of 2016, Ajit Singh Vs. Union of India.

entities.text: Ajit Singh Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
16. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue-wise findings and determination are as under : -
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
OPP 17
. The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors.. Vs. Union of India Page no. 10 of 13

sentences.text:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".

sentences.text: To prove its case, the petitioners, through their counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Ajit Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, they have relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 18.10.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioners has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
19. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

20. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

21. In the case of Ajit Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) acquired through Award No. 25 of 2005-06 dated 06.02.2006 as Rs. 19,45,800/- per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/- per acre has been given.

There is no evidence LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors.. Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 13 on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ajit Singh (supra).

entities.text: Prem Singh & Ors.. Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for his land as was awarded in Ajit Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/- per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre.
22. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 23.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:-
(1) Fair Market value of land of petitioner @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (North-West) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors.. Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 13 land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.
The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2004/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2631 Bighas 04 Biswas land situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.
The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 25 of 2005-06 dated 06.02.2006 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2631 Bighas 04 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/- per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/- per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.
The ld. LAC has overlooked the facts while determining the market value of the said land, in as much as, if all the factors are taken together for assessing the market value of the land under acquisition, it shall be Rs.
1 crore per acre or at least Rs. 2000/- per square yard.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore, DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition Prem Singh Ors. (2505-06) vs Union Of India (K.S.Nagar, Patti ... on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76469977/
5 for enhancement of compensation.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
My issue-wise findings and determination are as under : -
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors.. Vs. Union of India Page no. 10 of 13
20. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
22. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
opennyai_summary.decision:
There is no evidence LAC no.66/2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Prem Singh & Ors.. Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 13 on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ajit Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for his land as was awarded in Ajit Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/- per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 23.
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:-
(1) Fair Market value of land of petitioner @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
